<description>
Motivation: Reduce the risk of accidental privacy leak happening when broadcasting non-privately a requested transaction that had been previously broadcast privately.

Background: During the initial phase of private broadcast implementation there were unforeseen instances when a private transaction could get broadcast non-privately (e.g. see #36277 #36330 #36309).

Currently known pathways:

- Re-submission through `submitpackage`
- Wallet-rebroadcast (when a private transaction is "picked up" by the wallet, and rebrodcast after 1-2 days)

Note that these are being addressed, but other, currently non-identified pathways cannot be excluded.

Change summary: Add a general, extra safeguard: whenever there is a transaction broadcast request, check if the given transaction has been previously broadcast privately, and if so, refuse to broadcast non-privately.

Transaction relay is not affected, as it should not be affected by private broadcast.  When we receive a previously private-broadcast transaction for the first time (it's not yet in our mempool), we relay it as any other relayed transaction. Behavior is unchanged in this regard.

Notes:

- Prerequisite: This is built on top of #36477, as keeping finished private broadcasts in the queue is a prerequisite for this change to work.
- This proposed change is not an alternative to the use-case specific safeguards, but a complementary one.
- Testing currently uses the two pathways listed above. When they are closed, testing will be more difficult (i.e., it is hard to establish whether non-private broadcast is prevented by the use-case specific or the present generic guard).
- The private broadcast queue is not persisted, it doesn't survive node restarts
- Entries deleted via `abortprivatebroadcast` will be forgotten.
</description>

<commits>
35ebe832c5 private broadcast: show finished transactions in getprivatebroadcastinfo

For finished transactions, this allows the inspection of when and to
whom the transaction was sent as well as when/if it was echoed from
the network.

Co-authored-by: Vasil Dimov <vd@FreeBSD.org>

fa04f1e7b6 test: Add new private-then-public broadcast test via submitpackage

57fb0ee289 test: Add private-then-public broadcast test via wallet resend

Extend p2p_private_broadcast_then_public.py with a second case (if the
wallet is compiled): a wallet transaction is sent via private broadcast,
comes back from the network into the mempool and the wallet of the
originator, and is then announced to all peers by the periodic resend
of the wallet.

a100ddec89 net_processing: don't announce privately broadcast txs on request

With -privatebroadcast, sendrawtransaction sends the transaction only
via short-lived private broadcast connections and does not add it to
the mempool. However, other code paths can later add the same
transaction to the mempool and announce it to all peers, which links
the transaction to this node:
- the submitpackage RPC
- the wallet, on commit and on its periodic resend (e.g. after the
  transaction came back from the network and was picked up by the
  wallet)
- the GUI PSBT broadcast
- ReattemptInitialBroadcast(), for transactions in the unbroadcast set

All of these end up in PeerManager::InitiateTxBroadcastToAll(), which
is also used to relay transactions received from peers. Add a reason
parameter to it (RELAY or REQUESTED). If the reason is not RELAY and
the transaction is known to the private broadcast storage, then do not
announce it, remove it from the mempool's unbroadcast set, so that it
is not retried, and log that.

Relaying a privately broadcast transaction after it was received back
from the network is not affected: at that point the node behaves like
any other node that received the transaction.

Extend p2p_private_broadcast_then_public.py to check that re-sending
a privately broadcast transaction via submitpackage or via the periodic
resend of the wallet does not reach a public peer, while another
transaction sent the same way does.
</commits>

+P2P and network changes
+-----------------------
+
+- Transactions submitted via private broadcast are now retained after they are
+  received back from the network. This allows inspecting the state of such
+  transactions via the `getprivatebroadcastinfo` RPC. The information will now
+  not vanish as soon as the transaction is echoed from the network. In addition
+  `getprivatebroadcastinfo` returns a `received_by_us` object for echoed
+  transactions, containing the peer `address` and `time` of the reception. They
+  can be removed using the `abortprivatebroadcast` RPC, and are evicted oldest
+  first if the queue is full and room is needed for new transactions. (#36477)

 "summary": "Adds a guard in PeerManager to block non-private broadcasts of transactions that were previously broadcast privately. It introduces a reason parameter (relay versus requested broadcast) to InitiateTxBroadcastToAll, suppressing requested broadcasts and clearing mempool unbroadcast tracking when a transaction matches known private broadcasts. Normal relay of transactions received from network peers remains unaffected.",
 "problem": "Transactions broadcast via private broadcast can inadvertently be leaked to public peers later if re-submitted or re-broadcast through other mechanisms such as the submitpackage RPC, periodic wallet rebroadcasts, GUI PSBT broadcast, or mempool unbroadcast reattempts.",
 "card": "Prevents transactions sent via private broadcast from subsequently leaking origin identity through public broadcast paths. When transactions are re-submitted or rebroadcast via RPC, the wallet, or unbroadcast retry routines, PeerManager::InitiateTxBroadcastToAll would previously announce them to all connected peers. This change distinguishes requested broadcasts from standard peer relay, suppressing public announcements and clearing unbroadcast retry state if the transaction was previously tracked by private broadcast.
